test_title: RRB Group D 2025 Previous Year Numerical Qs Set - 01
subject: general
question: A real and inverted image is formed at a distance of 30 { cm} from a concave mirror when the object is placed 40 { cm} from the mirror. What will be the magnification produced by the mirror?
solution:
The correct answer is __**- 3/4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magnification (m)** produced by a spherical mirror gives the relative extent to which the image of an object is magnified with respect to the object size.
 
• It is expressed as the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object. It is also related to the **object distance (u)** and **image distance (v)** by the formula: **m = -v / u**.
 
• According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the **object distance (u)** is always **negative**. In this case, **u = - 40 cm**.
 
• Since the image is **real and inverted** and formed in front of the **concave mirror**, the **image distance (v)** is also **negative**. Here, **v = - 30 cm**.
 
• Substituting the values into the formula: **m = - (- 30) / (- 40)**. This simplifies to **m = 30 / (- 40)**, which equals **- 3/4**.
 
• The **negative sign** in the result signifies that the image is **real and inverted**. ***Hence, the correct answer is - 3/4.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror:** A spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is curved inwards (towards the center of the sphere). It is also known as a **converging mirror** because it converges light rays at a single point called the **focus**.
 
• **Sign Convention Rules:**
 
 
• The **Pole (P)** is taken as the origin.
 
• Distances measured in the direction of **incident light** are positive.
 
• Distances measured **opposite** to the direction of incident light are negative.
 
• Heights measured **upwards** and perpendicular to the principal axis are positive, while those measured **downwards** are negative.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Magnification:**
 
 
• If **m is negative**, the image is **real and inverted**.
 
• If **m is positive**, the image is **virtual and erect**.
 
• If **|m| > 1**, the image is **magnified** (larger than the object).
 
• If **|m| 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mirror Formula:** The relationship between **focal length (f)**, **object distance (u)**, and **image distance (v)** is given by **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**.
 
• In this specific question, since **|m| = 3/4 (0.75)**, which is less than **1**, the image is **diminished**.
 
• For a **concave mirror**, real images are always inverted, and virtual images (formed when the object is between the Focus and Pole) are always erect and magnified.
 
• The **radius of curvature (R)** is twice the **focal length (f)**, denoted as **R = 2f**.
